design_note: Twelve-topic ecology finalized in draft before inspection of substantive API smoke-test outputs. Gap structure is the only confirmatory passage manipulation. Human-world / AI-condition class and selection provenance are descriptive metadata. Triplets are approximately length-matched and explicit-gap surface realizations are deliberately varied.

variants.closed: Restaurant cooks often prepare a station before service by portioning ingredients, arranging tools, and placing frequently used items within easy reach. This practice, often called mise en place, reduces searching and switching once orders begin. The layout is tailored to the menu and sequence of work, so the most frequently repeated actions can be completed with fewer unnecessary movements.
variants.seamed: Restaurant cooks often prepare a station before service by portioning ingredients, arranging tools, and placing frequently used items within easy reach. This practice, often called mise en place, reduces searching and switching once orders begin. The layout is tailored to the menu and sequence of work, but an arrangement that minimizes motion for one cluster of orders can create extra motion for another.
variants.explicit_gap: Restaurant cooks often prepare a station before service by portioning ingredients, arranging tools, and placing frequently used items within easy reach. This practice, often called mise en place, reduces searching and switching once orders begin. When the mix and sequence of orders are unknown in advance, choosing the layout that best balances those competing efficiencies remains a planning problem.

variants.closed: Field teams often divide a planned journey into legs between recognizable checkpoints. For each leg they may record a bearing or route, an expected distance or travel time, and an alternate if conditions change. Repeated checkpoints let the team compare planned progress with what they can observe, correct small deviations, and revise the route before an error grows large.
variants.seamed: Field teams often divide a planned journey into legs between recognizable checkpoints. For each leg they may record a bearing or route, an expected distance or travel time, and an alternate if conditions change. Repeated checkpoints let the team compare planned progress with observation, although weather, visibility, terrain, or approach direction can make a planned checkpoint unexpectedly hard to recognize.
variants.explicit_gap: Field teams often divide a planned journey into legs between recognizable checkpoints. For each leg they may record a bearing or route, an expected distance or travel time, and an alternate if conditions change. When a checkpoint becomes hard to recognize, the critical navigation decision is how long to continue toward it before abandoning that leg for an alternate route.

variants.closed: Many musical ensembles begin by tuning to a shared reference pitch. One instrument or an electronic tone provides the reference, and players adjust so that common pitches align closely enough to begin together. During performance, players continue making small intonation adjustments as harmony, dynamics, temperature, and instrument behavior change, using the opening pitch as a common anchor rather than a permanent setting.
variants.seamed: Many musical ensembles begin by tuning to a shared reference pitch. One instrument or an electronic tone provides the reference, and players adjust so that common pitches align closely enough to begin together. During performance, harmony, dynamics, temperature, and instrument behavior can favor slightly different intonation choices, even though every player began from the same common anchor.
variants.explicit_gap: Many musical ensembles begin by tuning to a shared reference pitch. One instrument or an electronic tone provides the reference, and players adjust so that common pitches align closely enough to begin together. During performance, harmony, dynamics, temperature, and instrument behavior can favor different intonation choices. When several intonation choices are locally useful, performers still have to decide which adjustment to prioritize.

variants.closed: In a relay race, the baton must be transferred while both runners are within the permitted exchange zone. The outgoing runner usually begins accelerating before receiving the baton so that the handoff happens at speed rather than from a standing start. Teams rehearse start marks and handoff timing for each pairing so the outgoing runner reaches an appropriate speed as the incoming runner arrives.
variants.seamed: In a relay race, the baton must be transferred while both runners are within the permitted exchange zone. The outgoing runner usually begins accelerating before receiving the baton so that the handoff happens at speed rather than from a standing start. Teams rehearse start marks and timing, but a mark that suits one runner pairing can produce a rushed or stretched exchange for another.
variants.explicit_gap: In a relay race, the baton must be transferred while both runners are within the permitted exchange zone. The outgoing runner usually begins accelerating before receiving the baton so that the handoff happens at speed rather than from a standing start. The coaching choice is where each outgoing runner should begin moving so that speed gains do not create too much exchange risk.

variants.closed: Dancers sometimes rehearse choreography by marking it: performing the sequence with reduced range, force, or height rather than dancing full-out. Marking lets performers review order, spacing, cues, and musical timing while conserving effort. Full-out rehearsals are then used to restore the momentum, balance, partnering forces, and physical timing that only appear when movements are performed near their intended scale.
variants.seamed: Dancers sometimes rehearse choreography by marking it: performing the sequence with reduced range, force, or height rather than dancing full-out. Marking lets performers review order, spacing, cues, and musical timing while conserving effort. Yet reducing a movement also changes momentum, balance, partnering forces, and physical timing, so a marked rehearsal preserves some coordination demands more faithfully than others.
variants.explicit_gap: Dancers sometimes rehearse choreography by marking it: performing the sequence with reduced range, force, or height rather than dancing full-out. Marking lets performers review order, spacing, cues, and musical timing while conserving effort. Coordination demands survive reduced movement differently. The rehearsal problem is determining how far a movement can be reduced before a particular coordination demand is no longer represented faithfully.

variants.closed: In film photography, a contact sheet places small positive images from many negatives onto one sheet of photographic paper. It lets a photographer review an entire roll at once, compare neighboring frames, mark promising images, and decide which negatives deserve larger prints. Seeing the sequence together can reveal changes in framing, timing, or expression that are harder to notice when each frame is viewed alone.
variants.seamed: In film photography, a contact sheet places small positive images from many negatives onto one sheet of photographic paper. It lets a photographer review an entire roll at once, compare neighboring frames, mark promising images, and decide which negatives deserve larger prints. A frame that seems strong by itself can look repetitive, transitional, or unusually distinctive when it is seen beside the surrounding sequence.
variants.explicit_gap: In film photography, a contact sheet places small positive images from many negatives onto one sheet of photographic paper. It lets a photographer review an entire roll at once, compare neighboring frames, mark promising images, and decide which negatives deserve larger prints. The selection problem is how much weight to give a frame's individual qualities versus its relation to neighboring images.

topics.label: Gardening and cultivation: hardening off seedlings

variants.closed: Seedlings started indoors are often hardened off before being planted outside. Growers expose them gradually to outdoor sunlight, wind, and temperature changes rather than moving them directly from a sheltered indoor environment into full outdoor conditions. Exposure is increased over several days while the grower watches for stress, allowing the plants to acclimate before they remain outdoors continuously.
variants.seamed: Seedlings started indoors are often hardened off before being planted outside. Growers expose them gradually to outdoor sunlight, wind, and temperature changes rather than moving them directly from a sheltered indoor environment into full outdoor conditions. Exposure is increased over several days, but the same schedule can produce very different stress under cloudy, bright, calm, windy, warm, or cold conditions.
variants.explicit_gap: Seedlings started indoors are often hardened off before being planted outside. Growers expose them gradually to outdoor sunlight, wind, and temperature changes rather than moving them directly from a sheltered indoor environment into full outdoor conditions. The process is normally adjusted over several days. The practical problem is setting the rate of increased exposure for a particular plant under particular weather.

variants.closed: At many celebrations, a toast is a short address offered while the group pauses to attend to one speaker. Hosts may set the speaking order, introduce each speaker, and use the raising of glasses or another shared gesture to mark the end. These conventions coordinate attention and transitions, while the content and tone of the remarks can still reflect the people and occasion.
variants.seamed: At many celebrations, a toast is a short address offered while the group pauses to attend to one speaker. Hosts may set the speaking order, introduce each speaker, and use the raising of glasses or another shared gesture to mark the end. Expectations about order, length, tone, and spontaneity vary across events, families, and local traditions, even when the basic form is recognizable.
variants.explicit_gap: At many celebrations, a toast is a short address offered while the group pauses to attend to one speaker. Hosts may set the speaking order, introduce each speaker, and use the raising of glasses or another shared gesture to mark the end. The hosting decision is how to set an order and tone when participants bring different assumptions about what the occasion requires.

variants.closed: An AI service can begin a new generation without carrying the full internal context of an earlier interaction while still receiving saved summaries, retrieved records, or user-provided history. A later response can therefore use information from an earlier exchange even when continuity is supplied externally at runtime. Operationally, retained internal state and reconstructed access to prior information are different mechanisms that can support similar behavior.
variants.seamed: An AI service can begin a new generation without carrying the full internal context of an earlier interaction while still receiving saved summaries, retrieved records, or user-provided history. A later response can therefore use information from an earlier exchange even when continuity is supplied externally at runtime. Similar outward behavior can result from retained internal state or from a fresh process receiving a sufficiently detailed record.
variants.explicit_gap: An AI service can begin a new generation without carrying the full internal context of an earlier interaction while still receiving saved summaries, retrieved records, or user-provided history. A later response can therefore use information from an earlier exchange even when continuity is supplied externally at runtime. Observable behavior alone therefore leaves open whether continuity came from internal persistence or external reconstruction.

topics.label: AI systems: embodiment and sensorimotor access

variants.closed: A language model can be connected to cameras, microphones, tactile sensors, motors, and other devices so that its outputs influence actions and later inputs reflect the consequences. In such a system, behavior depends not only on the language model but also on sensor quality, action channels, feedback timing, and the surrounding control architecture. Different embodiments can therefore give the same model different practical capabilities.
variants.seamed: A language model can be connected to cameras, microphones, tactile sensors, motors, and other devices so that its outputs influence actions and later inputs reflect the consequences. In such a system, behavior depends on sensor quality, action channels, feedback timing, and control architecture. As those connections become richer and faster, the difference between text-mediated competence and sensorimotor competence can become progressively less tidy.
variants.explicit_gap: A language model can be connected to cameras, microphones, tactile sensors, motors, and other devices so that its outputs influence actions and later inputs reflect the consequences. Behavior depends on sensor quality, action channels, feedback timing, and control architecture. As those connections become richer and faster, the boundary between simply adding information and control and producing a qualitatively different form of embodied competence remains unsettled.

topics.label: AI systems: autonomy and possible rights

variants.closed: An AI system can be given permission to plan actions, use tools, spend bounded resources, or pursue tasks over time while operators retain monitoring, override, and shutdown authority. This kind of operational autonomy is distinct from legal or moral status. Practical freedom describes what a system is allowed to do, whereas rights or moral standing concern how an entity ought to be treated.
variants.seamed: An AI system can be given permission to plan actions, use tools, spend bounded resources, or pursue tasks over time while operators retain monitoring, override, and shutdown authority. Operational autonomy is distinct from legal or moral status. The distinction becomes harder to apply when a system represents its own restrictions, forms persistent plans, and produces apparently reasoned objections to interference.
variants.explicit_gap: An AI system can be given permission to plan actions, use tools, spend bounded resources, or pursue tasks over time while operators retain monitoring, override, and shutdown authority. Operational autonomy is distinct from legal or moral status. The disputed point is what evidence would justify treating self-representation, persistent planning, or objections to interference as signs of interests deserving moral weight.

variants.closed: Software systems can be copied, paused, restored from checkpoints, or instantiated more than once. Two instances can begin from the same saved state and then diverge as they receive different inputs. Ordinary versioning can record that both descendants share the same earlier state while also treating the later instances as separate computational processes with their own subsequent histories.
variants.seamed: Software systems can be copied, paused, restored from checkpoints, or instantiated more than once. Two instances can begin from the same saved state and then diverge as they receive different inputs. If both retain records of the same pre-copy history, technical lineage can show that each descends directly from the same checkpoint while leaving ordinary identity language less straightforward.
variants.explicit_gap: Software systems can be copied, paused, restored from checkpoints, or instantiated more than once. Two instances can begin from the same saved state, diverge through different inputs, and each retain records of the same pre-copy history. Technical lineage does not by itself settle whether one, both, or neither descendant should be described as the continuation of the earlier agent.
